name: Baal-hanan
overview: Baal-hanan was a male figure known as the Gederite who held responsibility over King David's olive and sycamore trees. While his tribal affiliation and family background are not detailed in Scripture, his role indicates a trusted position within David's administration. No additional notes are provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Baal-hanan means 'Baal is gracious,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This designation appears in 1 Chronicles 27:27 and does not indicate that the name was given by God. The meaning highlights a common ancient practice of invoking Baal in personal names, though the biblical text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Baal-hanan beyond his identification as a Gederite and his administrative role. There are no listed relatives or connections documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Baal-hanan's significance lies in his administrative oversight of valuable agricultural resources during King David's reign, as noted in 1 Chronicles 27:28. This responsibility underscores the organized governance under David and the trust placed in individuals like Baal-hanan to manage key aspects of the kingdom's economy. Though a minor figure, his role contributes to the broader picture of David's leadership and stewardship.
